538	uip is connectors list --output json
539	```
540	
541	Run `uip is connections --help` or `uip is resources --help` for all options.
542	
543	---
544	
545	## Bindings — top-level `.flow` `bindings[]`
546	
547	When a flow uses connector nodes, the runtime needs to know **which authenticated connection** to use for each connector. Bindings are authored in the flow's **top-level `bindings[]` array** (a sibling of `nodes`, `edges`, `definitions`). At `flow debug` / `flow pack` time the CLI regenerates `content/bindings_v2.json` from these entries.
548	
549	> **Never edit `bindings_v2.json` directly.** Any manual edits are overwritten on the next debug/pack. All authoring flows through the `.flow` file's top-level `bindings[]`.
550	
551	### How connector nodes reference bindings
552	
553	The connector node's **definition** (the manifest copied from `uip maestro flow registry get` into `definitions[]`) carries a `model.context[]` template like this. **Leave the definition exactly as the registry returns it** — do NOT rewrite `<bindings.*>` placeholders inside the definition, and do NOT author `model.context[]` on the instance:
554	
555	```json
556	"context": [
557	  { "name": "connectorKey", "type": "string", "value": "uipath-atlassian-jira" },
558	  { "name": "connection", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.uipath-atlassian-jira connection>" },
559	  { "name": "folderKey", "type": "string", "value": "<bindings.FolderKey>" }
560	]
561	```
562	
563	At BPMN emit time, the runtime rewrites each `<bindings.{name}>` placeholder to `=bindings.{id}` by finding a top-level `bindings[]` entry whose `name` matches the placeholder. For connectors the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is typically unset, so matching is **name-only** within the `resource: "Connection"` candidate set.
564	
565	> **Matching differs from resource nodes.** For `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl), the definition's `model.bindings.resourceKey` is set to `<FolderPath>.<ResourceName>`, so placeholder matching is scoped by `(name, resourceKey)`. For connector nodes, `resourceKey` on the definition is typically unset, so matching is name-only — the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder must be unique per connector in the flow. Don't confuse the two patterns.
566	
567	### Top-level `bindings[]` shape (CLI-emitted; reference only)
568	
569	`uip maestro flow node configure` populates these entries — you do not author them by hand. The schema below is the shape the CLI emits, for **inspection** when debugging a flow's binding state and as the planned shape for the **No-Live-Tenant** flow's sidecar `<nodeId>.detail.json` (see § No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration above). Per the [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) rules, `bindings[]` is part of the CLI-owned envelope for connector / connector-trigger / managed HTTP nodes.
570	
571	For every unique connection used in the flow, `node configure` appends **two entries** to top-level `bindings[]`:
572	
573	```json
574	"bindings": [
575	  {
576	    "id": "<CONN_BINDING_ID>",
577	    "name": "<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection",
578	    "type": "string",
579	    "resource": "Connection",
580	    "resourceKey": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
581	    "default": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
582	    "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId"
583	  },
584	  {
585	    "id": "<FOLDER_BINDING_ID>",
586	    "name": "FolderKey",
587	    "type": "string",
588	    "resource": "Connection",
589	    "resourceKey": "<CONNECTION_UUID>",
590	    "default": "<FOLDER_KEY>",
591	    "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey"
592	  }
593	]
594	```
595	
596	| Field | Value |
597	|-------|-------|
598	| `id` | Unique string within the file. Descriptive (e.g. `bJiraConn`) or short random (e.g. `bKEFLMRB2`). |
599	| `name` (connection binding) | The IS connection name (e.g. `"chandu.lella@uipath.com #3"`). `uip maestro flow node configure` fetches this from IS automatically — this is the supported path. The placeholder form `"<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection"` appears in the table for reference only (e.g. when inspecting a flow whose bindings have not yet been configured); it must match the definition's `model.context[].connection` placeholder (without the `<bindings.` prefix and `>` suffix). |
600	| `name` (folder binding) | Literal `"FolderKey"` — matches `<bindings.FolderKey>`. |
601	| `type` | Always `"string"`. |
602	| `resource` | Always `"Connection"` — capital C, case-sensitive. |
603	| `resourceKey` | The connection UUID from `uip is connections list`. **Same UUID on both bindings.** |
604	| `default` | Connection binding → connection UUID. Folder binding → folder key. |
605	| `propertyAttribute` | `"ConnectionId"` or `"FolderKey"` — case matters. |
606	
607	The connector node instance carries no `model` block and no binding/context data. `uip maestro flow node configure` populates only `inputs.detail` on the instance and writes the two top-level `bindings[]` entries — claiming the empty `ConnectionId` stub that `node add` hoisted (matched by name) and adding the `FolderKey` row. The connection UUID is held on the binding entry (`resourceKey`), not on the node.
608	
609	> **An empty-keyed Connection binding is a defect, not a cosmetic nit.** A `bindings[]` row with `resource: "Connection"`, `propertyAttribute: "ConnectionId"`, and `resourceKey: ""` faults Studio Web at runtime with `Value cannot be null. (Parameter 'Connection')`. `node add` hoists exactly one such stub (`name: "<connector-key> connection"`); `node configure` **claims it in place** (matching by that name), so a fully configured connector leaves no empty row — do not expect a "duplicate" empty pair, and never hand-edit `bindings[]` to remove one (it is CLI-owned). The only legitimate empty stub is the No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration case above, where the node is deliberately left unconfigured and the flow is known not to pass `flow validate` yet. An empty stub that survives a real `node configure` — or lingers after a connector node is removed — is a CLI bug to report, not something to paper over by hand.
610	
611	**Share bindings across nodes using the same connection.** If two connector nodes share the same `<CONNECTION_UUID>`, reuse the same two binding entries — do not add duplicates. Matching is by `name` only (the `<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection` placeholder is unique per connector), so any node whose definition resolves against `<bindings.<CONNECTOR_KEY> connection>` picks up the shared binding pair.
612	
613	### Single-connector example (Jira)
614	
615	```json
616	"bindings": [
617	  {
618	    "id": "bJiraConn",
619	    "name": "uipath-atlassian-jira connection",
620	    "type": "string",
621	    "resource": "Connection",
622	    "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
623	    "default": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
624	    "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId"
625	  },
626	  {
627	    "id": "bJiraFolder",
628	    "name": "FolderKey",
629	    "type": "string",
630	    "resource": "Connection",
631	    "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
632	    "default": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890",
633	    "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey"
634	  }
635	]
636	```
637	
638	### Multi-connector example (Jira + Slack)
639	
640	Two unique connections → four entries in `bindings[]` (two per connection):
641	
642	```json
643	"bindings": [
644	  { "id": "bJiraConn",   "name": "uipath-atlassian-jira connection",   "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "default": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId" },
645	  { "id": "bJiraFolder", "name": "FolderKey",                          "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e", "default": "folder-uuid-for-jira",                "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey" },
646	  { "id": "bSlackConn",  "name": "uipath-salesforce-slack connection", "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "default": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "propertyAttribute": "ConnectionId" },
647	  { "id": "bSlackFolder","name": "FolderKey",                          "type": "string", "resource": "Connection", "resourceKey": "a1b2c3d4-e5f6-7890-abcd-ef1234567890", "default": "folder-uuid-for-slack",               "propertyAttribute": "FolderKey" }
648	]
649	```
650	
651	Both `FolderKey` entries share the same `name` but have distinct `resourceKey`s — that's how the runtime keeps them separate.
652	
653	### Generated `bindings_v2.json` (reference only — do not edit)
654	
655	At debug/pack time, the CLI derives `content/bindings_v2.json` from the top-level `bindings[]` above. One `Connection` resource per unique `resourceKey`; the `FolderKey` bindings are absorbed as metadata (they do not produce standalone resource entries). The generated output looks like:
656	
657	```json
658	{
659	  "version": "2.0",
660	  "resources": [
661	    {
662	      "resource": "Connection",
663	      "key": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
664	      "id": "Connection7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
665	      "value": {
666	        "ConnectionId": {
667	          "defaultValue": "7622a703-5d85-4b55-849b-6c02315b9e6e",
668	          "isExpression": false,
669	          "displayName": "my-jira-connection"
670	        }
671	      },
672	      "metadata": {
673	        "ActivityName": "Create Issue",
674	        "BindingsVersion": "2.2",
675	        "DisplayLabel": "my-jira-connection",
676	        "UseConnectionService": "true",
677	        "Connector": "uipath-atlassian-jira"
678	      }
679	    }
680	  ]
681	}
682	```
683	
684	- `id` is always `"Connection" + <resourceKey>` (concatenated, no separator) — generated, not authored.
685	- `metadata.Connector` is derived from the definition's `model.context[].connectorKey`.
686	- `metadata.ActivityName` comes from the matched node's `display.label`.
687	
688	### Other binding resource types (triggers, queues, scheduled)
689	
690	For connector-trigger flows, the same pattern applies — top-level `bindings[]` entries with additional metadata; the CLI derives `EventTrigger` and `Property` resources for `bindings_v2.json`. See [connector-trigger/impl.md](../connector-trigger/impl.md) for the trigger-specific shape.
691	
692	| Generated `bindings_v2.json` resource | Authored via | Key source fields |
693	|---------------------------------------|--------------|-------------------|
694	| `Connection` | Top-level `bindings[]` with `resource: "Connection"`, `propertyAttribute: "ConnectionId"` | Covered above |
695	| `EventTrigger` | Top-level `bindings[]` + the trigger node itself | See connector-trigger plugin |
696	| `Property` | Trigger node's `model.inputs.filterFields` | See connector-trigger plugin |
697	| `Queue` / `TimeTrigger` | Specific trigger types | See relevant trigger plugin |
698	
699	> **Never hardcode connection IDs.** Always fetch them from IS at authoring time. Connection IDs are tenant-specific and change across environments.
700	
701	---
702	
703	## Debug
704	
705	### Common Errors
706	
707	| Error | Cause | Fix |
708	| --- | --- | --- |
709	| No connection found | Connection not bound — top-level `bindings[]` missing or `resourceKey` doesn't match the node | Run Step 1 above to bind a connection; verify both entries (`ConnectionId` + `FolderKey`) are in the top-level `bindings[]` |
710	| Connection ping failed | Connection expired or misconfigured | Re-authenticate the connection in the IS portal |
711	| Missing `inputs.detail` | Node added but not configured | Run `uip maestro flow node configure` with the detail JSON (Step 6) |
712	| Reference field has display name instead of ID | `uip is resources run list` was skipped | Resolve the reference field to get the actual ID (Step 4) |
713	| Node faults at runtime with "resource not found" or similar after a clean build and validate | Reference field uses an ID scoped to a **different** connection (common when copying from a prior flow in the same session — e.g., a Slack channel ID from workspace A pasted into a node bound to workspace B's connection) | Re-run `uip is resources run list "<connector-key>" "<objectName>" --connection-id <CURRENT_CONNECTION_ID>`, extract the fresh ID, update `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` in `--detail`, re-run `node configure`, re-debug. See Step 4 and the top-level Anti-Pattern on reference-ID reuse in [SKILL.md](../../../../../SKILL.md). |
714	| Required field missing at runtime | Required input field not provided | Check metadataFile for all `required: true` fields in both `requestFields` and `parameters` |
715	| `$vars` expression unresolvable | Node outputs block missing or node not connected | Verify the node has edges and upstream outputs are correctly referenced |
716	| `connectorMethodInfo` missing method/path | Used `registry get` without `--connection-id` | Re-run with `--connection-id` for enriched metadata (Step 2) |
717	| `bindings_v2.json` malformed or stale | It was hand-edited (the CLI overwrites edits on next debug/pack), or top-level `bindings[]` was mutated by hand | Never edit `bindings_v2.json` directly. Re-run `uip maestro flow node configure` on the affected connector node(s) so the CLI re-emits top-level `bindings[]`; `bindings_v2.json` is regenerated from those at the next debug/pack. Compare the emitted shape against the CLI-emitted reference in § Top-level `bindings[]` shape. |
718	| Connector key not found | Wrong key name | Run `uip is connectors list --output json` — keys are often prefixed with `uipath-` |
719	| FilterBuilder UI shows `undefined` when activity is reopened in Studio Web; flow runs at debug | A raw `queryParameters.<filterParamName>` string was passed instead of a structured filter tree, so `essentialConfiguration.savedFilterTrees.<filterParamName>` is empty. The runtime side works but Studio Web has no tree to render. | Re-run `uip maestro flow node configure` with `--detail '{"filter": {...tree...}}'` — the CLI populates both halves. See Step 6a above and [uipath-platform — Filter Trees (CEQL)](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/activities.md#filter-trees-ceql). |
720	| `node configure` fails with `'<name>' is a FilterBuilder parameter — pass a structured filter tree under --detail.filter` | Same root cause — raw string under `queryParameters` for a FilterBuilder param | Move the value into `--detail.filter` as a structured tree. The CLI catches this at configure time so it never reaches Studio Web. |
721	| Data Service query returns every record (or faults with malformed CEQL ending in `AND`) though a filter tree was configured; `node configure` reported Success | A filter-tree leaf's field id did not match the entity schema (matching is case-sensitive). The compiler drops unmatched leaves without an error — one bad leaf empties the query string, a bad leaf beside a good one leaves a dangling `AND`. | Compare the tree's field ids against the entity schema — `uip df entities list --output json` for the entity `Id`, then `uip df entities get <entity-id> --output json` for the field names. Re-run `node configure` with the exact ids. See Step 6a. |
722	| Node faults `[102003] Integration Services bad request`, IS 400 `"Expected a field name expression but got 'StringValue'"` — `flow validate` passed | Hand-authored CEQL string (e.g. Data Service `queryExpression`) quotes the **field name**: `'accountNumber' = '...'`. CEQL reads a quoted token as a string literal. Only `node configure --detail.filter` builds the expression for you; a string hand-written into the `.flow` JSON reaches IS unchecked. | Field names bare, only values quoted: `` `accountNumber = '${$vars...}'` ``. Or author via `--detail.filter` so the CLI compiles the CEQL. |
723	| Node faults `[102003] Integration Services bad request`, IS 400 `"Unsupported value expression 'Column' on field '<field>'"` — `flow validate` passed | Hand-authored CEQL double-quotes the **value**, typically from a concatenation with escaped quotes: `` =js:"accountNumber = \"" + String(v) + "\"" ``. CEQL reads a double-quoted token as a column reference, not a string literal. | Single-quote the value inside the concatenation: `` =js:"accountNumber = '" + String($vars.<node>.output.<field>) + "'" ``. Or author via `--detail.filter`. See [Hand-authored CEQL strings](#hand-authored-ceql-strings). |
724	| Node faults `[102003] Integration Services bad request` and the filter uses `eq`, `ne`, `gt`, `ge`, `lt`, or `le` | OData aliases in a hand-authored CEQL string. CEQL accepts only symbol operators. | Replace with `=`, `!=`, `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`. See the alias table in [Hand-authored CEQL strings](#hand-authored-ceql-strings). |
725	| `node configure` fails with `customFieldsRequestDetails.parameterValues must be an array of [key, value] tuples, not an object map` | Wrote `parameterValues: {key: value}` (object map). Studio Web emits its `Map<string,string\|null>` as `Array.from(entries())` — tuples, not object | Convert to tuples: `[["key", "value"], ...]`. See Step 6c. |
726	| Custom fields fault at runtime with token unresolved | A `{token}` in `objectActions[].apiConfiguration.url` or `body` has no entry in `parameterValues` | Re-read the ObjectAction's `apiConfiguration` placeholders, add the missing tuple to `parameterValues`. CLI does not validate token coverage. |
727	| `node configure` fails with `customFieldsRequestDetails has unknown keys: ObjectActionName, ParameterValues` | PascalCase inner keys instead of camelCase | Use `objectActionName` / `parameterValues`. Studio Web emits camelCase; PascalCase is rejected. |
728	| Field rejected at runtime as unknown (e.g. `"unknown field 'fields.labels[*]'"`) after a clean `flow validate` | `[*]` was left in the `bodyParameters` / `queryParameters` / `pathParameters` key. `[*]` is an array marker from `requestFields[].name`, not part of the wire key. | Strip `[*]` from the key in your `--detail` payload, pass a `=js:` expression returning the array, and re-run `node configure`. Fields with `[*].` (segments after the `[*]`) are not authorable. See the array-fields table in Step 6b. |
729	| Array field round-trips empty after a clean `flow validate` | Literal JSON array authored for a `[*]` field — validates but does not bind | Author as `=js:` expression returning the array: `"users": "=js:(['U123ABC', 'U456DEF'])"`. See the array-fields table in Step 6b. |
730	
731	### Debug Tips
732	
733	1. **Always check top-level `bindings[]` in the `.flow` file** — connector nodes silently fail if a binding is missing or malformed. Compare against the CLI-emitted `bindings[]` shape documented above (§ Top-level `bindings[]` shape). Do not inspect `bindings_v2.json` as ground truth; it is regenerated from the `.flow` on every debug/pack.
734	2. **Compare inputs against metadataFile** — the full metadata (from `is resources describe`) has every field with types, descriptions, and whether it's required
735	3. **`flow validate` does NOT catch connector-specific issues** — validation only checks JSON schema and graph structure. Missing `inputs.detail` fields, wrong reference IDs, and expired connections are caught only at runtime (`flow debug`)
736	4. **If a connector key doesn't work** — list all connectors: `uip is connectors list --output json`. Keys are often prefixed with `uipath-`
737	5. **Query/path parameters** — some required parameters appear only in the metadataFile `parameters` section, not in `requestFields`. Check both.
738	6. **`node configure` populates bindings automatically** — it appends the two top-level `bindings[]` entries and populates `inputs.detail`. The generated `bindings_v2.json` follows from these at debug/pack time. If you cannot run `node configure` (no live tenant, sandbox forbids it, planning-only request), record the planned binding entries in the sidecar `<nodeId>.detail.json` per the No-Live-Tenant flow above — do not author `bindings[]` directly on the `.flow` as a substitute, and note that the flow will not pass `flow validate` until a real `node configure` runs.
739

1	# Loop Node — Implementation
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.logic.loop`
6	
7	## Registry Validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.loop --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input ports `input` and `loopBack`, output ports `success` and `output`, required input `collection`. Set the node instance `typeVersion` to the `version` field from this response — do not hardcode it.
14	
15	## JSON Structure
16	
17	### Loop node
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "id": "loop1",
22	  "type": "core.logic.loop",
23	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
24	  "display": { "label": "Loop over items" },
25	  "inputs": {
26	    "collection": "=js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items",
27	    "parallel": false
28	  }
29	}
30	```
31	
32	> **Collection source shape depends on the node type.** Connector `list` activities return the bare array — `"collection": "=js:$vars.searchIssuesByJql1.output"`, NOT `.output.issues` / `.output.items`. HTTP nodes differ — envelope preserved: `.output.body.<key>` as above. See [connector/impl.md — Connector output shape](../connector/impl.md).
33	
34	Set `"parallel": true` to execute all iterations concurrently.
35	
36	### Loop body nodes — `parentId` required
37	
38	Every node inside the loop body **must** have `"parentId"` set to the loop node's ID. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is part of the loop and variableUpdates will not fire per-iteration.
39	
40	```json
41	{
42	  "id": "processItem",
43	  "type": "core.action.script",
44	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
45	  "display": { "label": "Process item" },
46	  "inputs": {
47	    "script": "return $vars.product * $vars.loop1.currentItem"
48	  },
49	  "parentId": "loop1"
50	}
51	```
52	
53	> **Critical:** If you omit `parentId`, the node executes outside the loop context. State variables will not update across iterations and loop outputs like `currentItem` will be inaccessible.
54	
55	## Adding / Editing
56	
57	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Use the JSON structure above for the node-specific `inputs` and `parentId`.
58	
59	### CLI carve-out nodes inside a loop
60	
61	When adding a CLI carve-out node (connector, connector trigger, or managed HTTP) inside a loop, pass `--parent` to set `parentId` automatically:
62	
63	```bash
64	uip maestro flow node add <FLOW_PATH> core.action.http.v2 --label "Fetch data" --parent <LOOP_ID> --output json
65	uip maestro flow node add <FLOW_PATH> <CONNECTOR_NODE_TYPE> --label "Get record" --parent <LOOP_ID> --output json
66	```
67	
68	`--parent` validates the parent node exists and sets `parentId` on the new node. For non-carve-out node types (script, end, etc.), set `"parentId"` directly in the JSON — see the examples above.
69	
70	## Wiring
71	
72	Loop nodes have a specific wiring pattern:
73	
74	- `input` — entry from upstream
75	- `output` — into the loop body (first body node)
76	- `loopBack` — return from last body node back to loop
77	- `success` — exit after loop completes (to next downstream node)
78	
79	See [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md) for edge add procedures.
80	
81	## Accessing Loop Variables Inside Body
82	
83	Inside the loop body, access the current item via `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem`:
84	
85	```javascript
86	// In a Script node inside the loop body (parentId must be set to the loop node)
87	const item = $vars.loop1.currentItem;
88	const index = $vars.loop1.currentIndex;
89	return { processed: item.name.toUpperCase(), position: index };
90	```
91	
92	| Variable | Description |
93	| --- | --- |
94	| `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` | The item being processed in this iteration |
95	| `$vars.<loopId>.currentIndex` | 0-based iteration index |
96	| `$vars.<loopId>.collection` | The full collection being iterated |
97	
98	> **Do not use `iterator.currentItem`.** The correct access pattern is `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` where `<loopId>` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`).
99	
100	### Required node variables for loop outputs
101	
102	For `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` etc. to resolve, you must add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`:
103	
104	```json
105	{
106	  "variables": {
107	    "nodes": [
108	      {
109	        "id": "loop1.currentItem",
110	        "type": "any",
111	        "description": "The current item being iterated in the loop",
112	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentItem" }
113	      },
114	      {
115	        "id": "loop1.currentIndex",
116	        "type": "number",
117	        "description": "The current iteration index (0-based)",
118	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentIndex" }
119	      },
120	      {
121	        "id": "loop1.collection",
122	        "type": "array",
123	        "description": "The collection being iterated over",
124	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "collection" }
125	      },
126	      {
127	        "id": "loop1.output",
128	        "type": "array",
129	        "description": "Aggregated results from all loop iterations",
130	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "output" }
131	      }
132	    ]
133	  }
134	}
135	```
136	
137	## State Accumulation with variableUpdates
138	
139	To accumulate state across loop iterations (counters, running totals), use an `inout` variable with a `variableUpdate` on the body node:
140	
141	```json

If you need to compute using `currentItem`, do the computation in the script and reference the script's output in the variableUpdate.

170	A flow that iterates over a collection, accumulates a result in an `inout` variable via a Script body node, and outputs the final value.

176	      "id": "start",
177	      "type": "core.trigger.manual",
178	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
179	      "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },

181	    },

184	      "type": "core.logic.loop",

196	      },

207	      }

211	    { "id": "e1", "sourceNodeId": "start", "sourcePort": "output", "targetNodeId": "loop1", "targetPort": "input" },
212	    { "id": "e2", "sourceNodeId": "loop1", "sourcePort": "output", "targetNodeId": "bodyScript", "targetPort": "input" },
213	    { "id": "e3", "sourceNodeId": "bodyScript", "sourcePort": "success", "targetNodeId": "loop1", "targetPort": "loopBack" },
214	    { "id": "e4", "sourceNodeId": "loop1", "sourcePort": "success", "targetNodeId": "end1", "targetPort": "input" }
215	  ],
216	  "variables": {
217	    "globals": [
218	      { "id": "inputItems", "direction": "in", "type": "array", "defaultValue": [] },
219	      { "id": "accumulator", "direction": "inout", "type": "number", "defaultValue": 0 },
220	      { "id": "result", "direction": "out", "type": "number" }
221	    ],
222	    "nodes": [
223	      { "id": "loop1.currentItem", "type": "any", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentItem" } },
224	      { "id": "loop1.currentIndex", "type": "number", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentIndex" } },
225	      { "id": "loop1.collection", "type": "array", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "collection" } },
226	      { "id": "loop1.output", "type": "array", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "output" } },
227	      { "id": "bodyScript.output", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "bodyScript", "outputId": "output" } },
228	      { "id": "bodyScript.error", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "bodyScript", "outputId": "error" } }
229	    ],
230	    "variableUpdates": {
231	      "bodyScript": [

233	      ]
234	    }
235	  }
236	}

239	Key points in this pattern:
240	- `bodyScript` has `"parentId": "loop1"` — places it inside the loop
241	- Script accesses `$vars.loop1.currentItem` for the current iteration value
242	- `variableUpdate` on `bodyScript` writes the script's return value back to `accumulator`
243	- `accumulator` is `inout` so it persists across iterations
244	- End node maps the final accumulated value to the `out` variable

326	## Debug
327	
328	| Error | Cause | Fix |
329	| --- | --- | --- |
330	| Collection is empty or null | Expression evaluates to null/undefined | Check `collection` expression and upstream output |
331	| `$vars.loop1.currentItem` is undefined | Missing node variable binding or missing `parentId` | Add `loop1.currentItem` to `variables.nodes` and set `parentId` on body nodes |
332	| State variable not updating across iterations | Body node missing `parentId` | Add `"parentId": "<loopId>"` to every node inside the loop body |
333	| State variable becomes `NaN` | variableUpdate expression uses `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` | Loop variables are not available in variableUpdate expressions. Do the computation in the script and reference `$vars.<bodyNodeId>.output` in the variableUpdate |
334	| Infinite loop | Edges wired incorrectly | Ensure only `loopBack` creates the cycle, not arbitrary edges |
335	| No output after loop | Missing `success` edge | Wire the `success` port to the next downstream node |

1	# Loop Node — Planning
2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.logic.loop`
6	
7	## When to Use
8	
9	Use a Loop node to iterate over a collection of items. Supports sequential and parallel execution.
10	
11	### Selection Heuristics
12	
13	| Situation | Use Loop? |
14	| --- | --- |
15	| Process each item in an array | Yes |
16	| Run the same operation on multiple inputs concurrently | Yes (with `parallel: true`) |
17	| Simple data transformation on a collection | No — use [Transform](../transform/planning.md) |
18	| Distribute work items to robots | No — use [Queue](../queue/planning.md) |
19	
20	## Ports
21	
22	| Input Port(s) | Output Port(s) |
23	| --- | --- |
24	| `input`, `loopBack` | `success`, `output`, `error` |
25	
26	- `loopBack` — receives the edge returning from the last node inside the loop body
27	- `success` — fires after all iterations complete
28	- `output` — carries aggregated results from all iterations
29	- `error` — implicit error port shared with all action nodes; fires when the loop or an iteration throws. See [Implicit error port on action nodes](../../../../shared/file-format.md#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes).
30	
31	## Key Inputs
32	
33	| Input | Required | Description |
34	| --- | --- | --- |
35	| `collection` | Yes | Expression pointing to an array (e.g., `$vars.fetchData.output.body.items`) |
36	| `parallel` | No | `true` to execute all iterations concurrently (default: sequential) |
37	
38	## Loop Variables (available inside loop body only)
39	
40	- `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` — the item being processed in this iteration
41	- `$vars.<loopId>.currentIndex` — 0-based iteration index
42	- `$vars.<loopId>.collection` — the full collection
43	
44	Where `<loopId>` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`).
45	
46	## Wiring Rules
47	
48	- The loop body starts from the `output` port of the loop node
49	- The last node in the loop body connects back to the loop's `loopBack` port
50	- After all iterations, execution continues from the `success` port
51	- Do not create cycles except through the `loopBack` mechanism
52	- **Every node inside the loop body must have `"parentId": "<loopId>"`** — without this, variableUpdates will not fire per-iteration and loop variables will be inaccessible

2	
3	The `.flow` file is a JSON document at `<ProjectName>.flow` in the project root. It is the **only file you should edit** — other generated files will be overwritten.
4	
5	## Table of contents
6	
7	- [Top-level structure](#top-level-structure)
8	- [Project structure (generated scaffold)](#project-structure-generated-scaffold)
9	- [Node instance](#node-instance)
10	- [Layout](#layout)
11	- [Edge — both ports required](#edge--both-ports-required)
12	- [Definition entry](#definition-entry)
13	- [Common node types](#common-node-types)
14	- [Standard ports by node type](#standard-ports-by-node-type)
15	- [Implicit error port on action nodes](#implicit-error-port-on-action-nodes)
16	- [Minimal working example — dice roller](#minimal-working-example--dice-roller)
17	- [entry-points.json — auto-generated, do not edit](#entry-pointsjson--auto-generated-do-not-edit)
18	- [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings (top-level `bindings[]`)](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings)
19	- [Bindings — connector connection binding](#bindings--connector-connection-binding)
20	
21	## Top-level structure
22	
23	```json
24	{
25	  "id": "<uuid>",
26	  "version": "<scaffolded file-format version>",
27	  "name": "MyFlow",
28	  "nodes": [],
29	  "edges": [],
30	  "definitions": [],
31	  "bindings": [],
32	  "variables": {},
33	  "layout": {
34	    "nodes": {}
35	  }
36	}
37	```
38	
39	> **Key order is NOT guaranteed — never anchor edits on it.** The skeleton above is illustrative; the CLI does not commit to a stable top-level key sequence or to which optional keys are present. Real flows vary: `runtime` may appear (and has been observed *before* `nodes`, not after `definitions`) or be absent entirely; `bindings`, `variables`, `solutionId`, `projectId`, and a trailing `metadata` object surface in different positions depending on CLI version and what the flow contains. When editing a `.flow`, anchor each `Edit` on the **target array's own key** (`"nodes": [`, `"edges": [`, `"definitions": [`, or `layout.nodes`) located in the text you just `Read` — never on "the key that follows X." See [greenfield.md — Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits](../author/references/greenfield.md#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order).
40	
41	Optional top-level `runtime`: a CLI-managed object that appears on some flows (e.g. after `uip maestro flow node add` for an HTTP/connector node) and is absent on others. It is not user-authored — do not add, remove, or anchor on it. Its presence and position are not guaranteed.
42	
43	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:start-->
44	**Top-level `version`** = workflow file-format version. **Use the exact value `uip maestro flow init` scaffolds** — do not hand-pick, hardcode, or downgrade it. It is not a semver string; the schema gates on an exact literal for the current file-format version, so an older value (e.g. `"1.0"`, `"1.0.0"`) that worked for a legacy parser will fail for a new flow. `init` always writes the accepted value; preserve it. To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`.
45	<!--skill-flavor:flow-format-version-source:end-->
46	
47	> **Don't confuse top-level `version` with `definitions[].version` / `typeVersion`.** Node-definition `version` (and matching node-instance `typeVersion`) are validated by `versionSchema`, a regex that accepts both `x.y` and `x.y.z` (`/^\d+\.\d+(\.\d+)?$/`, error `'Version must be in format "x.y" or "x.y.z"'`). Both layers are canonically `x.y`, but the node-level regex still accepts legacy 3-part strings so registry definitions (`"1.0"`) and older scaffolded nodes (`"1.0.0"`) both parse. The two layers report distinct errors, but Zod may collapse a node-level mismatch to path `(root)`. If you see a version-related error at `(root)`, audit the top-level `version` first; if it's correct, check each node's `typeVersion` against the matching `definitions[].version`.
48	
49	`solutionId` and `projectId` may also appear at the top level — these are auto-populated by the project scaffold and packaging. Preserve the generated values.
50	
51	> **`bindings[]`** holds Orchestrator resource references for `uipath.core.*` resource nodes (rpa, agent, flow, agentic-process, api-workflow, hitl) and for connector-node connections. See [Bindings — Orchestrator resource bindings](#bindings--orchestrator-resource-bindings-top-level-bindings) below and the [connector plugin](../author/references/plugins/connector/impl.md) for the connector-binding shape.
52	
53	## Project structure (generated scaffold)
54	
55	```
56	<ProjectName>/
57	├── project.uiproj          # { "Name": "...", "ProjectType": "Flow" }
58	├── <ProjectName>.flow      # ← edit this
59	├── bindings_v2.json        # resource bindings
60	├── entry-points.json       # input/output schema declarations
61	├── operate.json            # runtime options
62	└── package-descriptor.json # packaging manifest
63	```
64	
65	## Node instance
66	
67	```json
68	{
69	  "id": "rollDice",
70	  "type": "core.action.script",
71	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
72	  "display": { "label": "Roll Dice" },
73	  "inputs": {
74	    "script": "return { roll: Math.floor(Math.random() * 6) + 1 };"
75	  },
76	  "outputs": {
77	    "output": {
78	      "type": "object",
79	      "description": "The return value of the script",
80	      "source": "=result.response",
81	      "var": "output"
82	    },
83	    "error": {
84	      "type": "object",
85	      "description": "Error information if the script fails",
86	      "source": "=Error",
87	      "var": "error"
88	    }
89	  }
90	}
91	```
92	
93	**Required fields on every node**: `id`, `type`, `typeVersion`, **`display`** (with at least a `label`). This applies to **every** node — triggers (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers), action nodes, control-flow nodes (`core.control.end`, `core.logic.terminate`), and human-task nodes. The Zod `nodeSchema` declares `display: displayConfigSchema` without `.optional()`, so no node type is exempt — even ones that "feel" trivial.
94	
95	`typeVersion` must match the corresponding `definitions[].version` exactly. The registry often returns versions such as `"1.0"` while older examples or scaffolded files may show `"1.0.0"`. If a node uses `typeVersion: "1.0.0"` but the copied definition is `"version": "1.0"`, validation reports "Node type `<type>:1.0.0` has no matching definition." When direct-authoring a new node from `registry get`, set `typeVersion` to the copied definition's `version`; when preserving an existing node, preserve its existing node/definition pair unless you intentionally update both together. <!-- version-check-skip --> (explains the x.y vs x.y.z mismatch mechanic; literals are illustrative, not pinned)
96	
97	> **Gotcha — vague schema-validation error on missing `display`.** Omitting `display` on any node produces:
98	>
99	> ```
100	> [error] [(root)] Schema validation failed: Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
101	> ```
102	>
103	> The error path is `(root)` and does NOT pinpoint which node or which field is missing. If you see this error after editing a `.flow` file, audit every node for a `display` block before doing anything else.
104	
105	> **No instance `model` block.** BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, and binding/context templates all live in the node's **definition** (the manifest copied from the registry into `definitions[]`). The runtime hydrates them from the definition at serialization time — instances carry only per-instance data (`inputs`, `outputs`, `display`). This applies to every inline-agent-related node too: `uipath.agent.autonomous` plus every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) carries source identity at `inputs.source`. Their definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists that identity onto each instance's `inputs.source`. Do not write a `"model": { "source": ... }` block on the instance.
106	>
107	> **No `ui` block on nodes.** Position and size are stored in the top-level `layout` object, not on individual nodes. See [Layout](#layout) below.
108	
109	### Instance-specific identity fields
110	
111	A few per-instance identity fields live on the node instance:
112	
113	| Field | Used by | Purpose |
114	|-------|---------|---------|
115	| `inputs.entryPointId` | All trigger nodes (`core.trigger.manual`, `core.trigger.scheduled`, connector triggers) | Stable UUID identifying the entry point |
116	| `inputs.isDefaultEntryPoint` | Trigger nodes in subflows | Boolean marking the default entry point when a subflow has multiple triggers |
117	| `inputs.source` | `uipath.agent.autonomous` and every attached `uipath.agent.resource.*` node (tool, escalation, context) | For `uipath.agent.autonomous`: the inline agent's `projectId`. For resource nodes: the attached resource UUID. Definitions declare `model.source: true`; flow-core hoists onto the instance — no instance `model` block. |
118	| `inputs.color`, `inputs.content` | Sticky-note nodes | Visual content of the sticky note |
